instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Management consulting firm serving mid-market companies with strategy, operational excellence, and digital transformation engagements. Team of 40 consultants across 3 offices. Typical engagements are 8-16 weeks. Evaluating knowledge management AI to capture and surface past engagement insights for proposal development. We have a dedicated management team across core functions but operate with limited middle management layers. Budget cycles are annual with moderate flexibility for mid-year reallocation if a strong business case is presented. Innovation initiatives compete with day-to-day operational demands for team attention.
answers.pastInitiatives: Innovation is embedded in our operating rhythm. We run quarterly hackathons, maintain a formal patent portfolio, and have a rotating 'innovation fellow' program where high-potential employees spend 6 months dedicated to exploratory projects. Our last hackathon produced a prototype for automated quality inspection using computer vision that is now in production, reducing defect escape rate by 35%.
answers.strategicGoals: We are heavily dependent on a single product category and a concentrated customer base — our top 3 clients represent 55% of revenue. This concentration risk is unacceptable for our long-term health. We need to identify and develop new revenue streams, possibly including new product lines for different customer segments or entirely new business models that leverage our existing capabilities.
answers.teamSize: Our team includes 3 backend developers, 1 frontend developer, and 1 QA engineer, managed by the CTO who also acts as product owner. We outsource UI/UX design to a freelance designer as needed. The team can handle incremental product improvements but struggles to carve out focused time for larger innovation bets without compromising current sprint commitments.

input.changes_since_last: Post-merger integration underway. Team doubled to 3 members. Culture clash between legacy and new teams.

opportunities.title: De-risking Revenue through Vertical Market Expansion
opportunities.rationale: The extreme dependency on the top 3 clients (55% of revenue) presents an unacceptable concentration risk. This opportunity shifts focus from general diversification to identifying and developing specific, adjacent market segments that can absorb current expertise.

first_actions: Conduct a portfolio mapping exercise detailing core competencies applied to non-client industry verticals.
Identify the top 2 most underserved or high-growth vertical markets based on macro trends, not just current client needs.
Develop preliminary 'pillar' product concepts targeted at these identified new segments.
execution_plan.success_metric: Creation of a defined business case and pitch deck for the first non-client vertical market.
milestones: Completion of competitor analysis in 2 new verticals (Month 1)
Finalization of Minimum Viable Offering (MVO) scope for one target segment (Month 3)

opportunities.title: Standardizing Cross-Functional Knowledge Transfer Platform
opportunities.rationale: The limited middle management layers and post-merger culture clash are creating knowledge siloes. Implementing a structured platform to capture expertise (beyond just project final reports) will ensure continuity and accelerate onboarding for future growth.

first_actions: Map critical 'tribal' or undocumented processes currently held by high-performing individuals.
Pilot a knowledge base solution using the existing KM AI evaluation to capture specific domain expertise (e.g., implementation checklists, risk assessment models).
Integrate mandatory knowledge transfer checkpoints into project closeout rituals.
resources_needed: Dedicated time from subject matter experts (SMEs)
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in ramp-up time for new consultants on core services by 20%.
milestones: Knowledge base prototype operationalized with 3 key service lines (Month 2)
Mandatory knowledge documentation completed for all staff exiting major projects.

next_steps.action: The leadership team must allocate protected time and budget to run the market vertical mapping exercise (Oppo 1), treating it as a core strategic function, not an optional initiative.
CTO must institute a mandatory 'Innovation Block' of 10-15% time for development staff, ensuring this time is protected from day-to-day operational sprints to facilitate focused product work.
Conduct a formal, structured workshop focusing specifically on defining and role-playing the ideal post-merger operating model to bridge cultural gaps.

key_weaknesses: Extreme customer concentration risk (55% of revenue from top 3 clients).
Structural gap due to limited middle management, hindering scalable knowledge capture and mentorship.
Innovation efforts are highly vulnerable to operational priorities, leading to inconsistent focus time.

improvements: Successful completion of prior opportunities has created momentum and proof-of-concept assets (e.g., automated quality inspection prototype).
Formalization of innovation processes continues, demonstrating commitment despite operational pressures.
Clear identification of structural limits in the team's capacity for large bets.
persistent_gaps: Failure to systematize knowledge transfer across functional boundaries (tribal knowledge remains at risk).
The strategic imperative (diversification) has not yet translated into a fully budgeted and staffed new revenue stream.
Cultural friction from the merger continues to drain management attention.
achieved_milestones: Operationalizing automated quality inspection prototype in production, generating measurable cost savings.
Confirmed capacity for incremental product improvements (Backend/Frontend team structure defined).

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The company has successfully moved from conceptualizing solutions (hackathons) to operational deployment (production prototype). While significant execution progress was made, the underlying strategic risk (client concentration) and internal structural barriers remain the primary limiting factors.
